documents.title: A visit to the Pennwick lamp room
documents.content:
# Handling the demonstration lamps
Visitors sometimes mistake the small Veyra lamp for a pocket torch. Its body is made of blue enamelled steel, and a loop of cork protects the handle. The demonstration Veyra stands on the east windowsill, away from the curtain. It is a display object, so the keeper asks visitors to leave the switch alone.

The larger Neris lamp, across the room, has a copper body and a leather handle. It is used during the evening tour. Both lamps carry paper tags from the Pennwick lamp room; the tags are collection marks, not makers' labels. A locked cabinet holds spare glass chimneys. The room guide does not name the manufacturer of either lamp.

documents.title: Notes from Sedgebench workshop
documents.content:
The weekly tool circle meets behind Sedgebench workshop. Olin Vess coordinates the tool circle; his job is to arrange the workbenches and pair new members with experienced ones. The workshop itself is owned by Pell Arvo. Pell drops in on Saturdays but does not coordinate the circle.

For the autumn repair day, Olin asked ceramicist Nema Tull to demonstrate how to mend cracked plant pots. Nema teaches the pot-mending session. Tool sharpening is taught by Ruvan Silt, who also maintains the whetstones. Registration cards ask only for a preferred first name and a session choice. The workshop publishes no biographies of its instructors.

documents.title: How the Reedvale seed exchange is run
documents.content:
Reedvale Seed Exchange is a shared cupboard scheme, not a seed shop. The Tarrow Commons Association administers the exchange and keeps its membership register. Brookglass Library provides the cupboard space. Lending the space does not make the library the administrator.

New packet labels are printed by Duneleaf Press. Donors fill and seal envelopes at home. The Moorline Garden Guild supplies volunteer stewards during the spring swap. Stewards check that packets carry a crop name and harvest year; they do not certify germination. A visitor looking for research results should not treat the stamp on an envelope as a laboratory mark.

documents.title: Lowmere crossing: seasonal service note
documents.content:
# Calendar for the little ferry
The Lowmere ferry resumes public trips on 17 April 2027. Crew practice starts on 10 April 2027, but practice crossings do not take passengers. The final public trip of the season is scheduled for 28 September 2027.

On operating days, the first departure from the mill landing is at 08:20. The return timetable is posted at the opposite landing. This notice covers the season's boundaries and the first outward departure only. During a high-water closure, a board at the mill landing replaces the normal departure notice. The rowboat tied beside the ferry is reserved for the crew.

documents.title: Three gatherings at Vellum House
documents.content:
From the house diary:

On 6 May 2026, the map unveiling took place in the glass gallery. Dera Quill presented the river map, then left before the afternoon reading. The reading was a separate event held in the west attic on the same date; its speaker was poet Sovan Pell.

The bookbinding demonstration happened on 9 May 2026 in the courtyard. At that demonstration, binder Hesta Orm showed visitors how to sew a flexible spine. Rain ended the demonstration early, so the planned question period never began. The entry hall remained open for ordinary visits on both days. A display there advertises last year's map sale, which was not part of this week's gatherings.

documents.title: Claybank pantry packing card
documents.content:
A standard household parcel from Claybank Pantry contains three tins of beans and two bags of oats. Each oat bag weighs 750 grams. The tins are counted as units; this card does not give their individual weights.

Packers place six household parcels in each blue delivery crate. Red crates carry donated cooking equipment and must not be used for food parcels. An unusually large household may receive a second parcel, but volunteers should record that as two parcels rather than enlarging one. The packing table has room for four open crates. The storage shelf's printed number, 24, is a shelf identifier and is not an inventory count.

documents.title: Mossquay Desk Hall booking terms
documents.content:
Mossquay Desk Hall quotes its prices in crowns. A weekday day pass costs 18 crowns and includes tea. A Saturday day pass costs 24 crowns, with tea included on the same terms. Neither pass includes printing.

Reserving the quiet booth costs an additional 7 crowns per hour. The booth surcharge applies even when the guest already has a day pass. There is no charge for borrowing a pencil. Prices on the lobby's old launch poster are crossed out; that poster's 12-crown day pass is no longer offered. Guests who need longer access should speak to the desk about a separate arrangement. This page lists no monthly membership price.

documents.title: Words used on a Windrow repair ticket
documents.content:
# A short desk glossary
A bench hold is a pause in repair work while the customer decides whether to approve an estimate. It does not mean that a tool has been reserved for the customer to borrow.

A return slip is the paper receipt that identifies an item when its owner collects it. Staff attach the slip number to the workshop copy of the ticket. A trial run is a supervised test after a repair, performed before the item is handed back. The customer may watch from the marked floor line.

These are local desk terms. A phrase used by another repair shop may carry a different meaning. The glossary has no entry for a field seal, although older tickets sometimes have a box bearing that label.

documents.title: Hillwake observatory maintenance log
documents.content:
Tuesday's public viewing session was cancelled because grit had jammed the dome track. The telescope optics were clear. A delivery van had arrived late that morning, but the late delivery was not the reason for cancelling the session.

On Wednesday, the team moved the logbooks to the dry cabinet because water had seeped through a window seam. The window was sealed before evening. Thursday's camera test produced blurred frames because a loose bracket let the camera vibrate. Tightening that bracket restored sharp frames. A brief power flicker happened after the camera test had finished and did not affect those frames. The note records what failed and what was repaired; it makes no finding about the origin of the grit.

documents.title: Returning an Amberdock loan battery
documents.content:
Please use the staffed hatch to return a loan battery. First switch the battery off. Next fit its orange terminal cover. Then hand it to the hatch attendant together with the numbered loan card. Do not drop the battery into the book-return slot.

If the orange cover is missing, tell the attendant before handing over the battery; staff keep spare covers at the hatch. The attendant scans the loan card and gives you a return receipt. Keep that receipt until the loan disappears from your account. The hatch opens at noon on service days. This card is about ordinary returns and gives no instructions for transporting a damaged battery.

documents.title: Brindle roof garden visitor questions
documents.content: The Brindle roof garden opens for small guided visits. Entry is through the stair tower beside the bakery. The planter labels are renewed in spring; please leave loose labels with the guide. The answers below apply to ordinary visits, which last about forty minutes. Private workshops have their own booking notes.

faqs.question: Can I bring my dog?
faqs.answer: Dogs may enter the Brindle roof garden only during the Sunday morning visit.

faqs.question: Is there somewhere for a pushchair?
faqs.answer: Folded pushchairs can be left in the stair-tower alcove during a visit.

faqs.question: Do I have to print my booking?
faqs.answer: A booking code shown on a phone is accepted; a printed copy is optional.

faqs.question: Can I eat lunch in the garden?
faqs.answer: Food is allowed only on the benches beside the water tank. Please carry all wrappers back downstairs.

documents.title: A letter from Elmshoe cycle couriers
documents.content:
Customers sometimes ask what happens when a parcel cannot be delivered. If the recipient is absent, we take the parcel back to the Wren Street depot. We never leave an undelivered parcel in a neighbour's porch. A card through the door explains how the recipient can arrange another attempt.

If a parcel's address label has washed off, the parcel goes to the inspection desk. Staff open a tracing request there without opening the parcel itself. Fragile parcels travel in padded green boxes. The green boxes return with the riders after delivery and remain the property of the courier cooperative. The riders' yellow bags are for letters, not fragile parcels.

documents.title: Ornfield museum: access and facilities
documents.content:
The ticket desk has been asked to clarify several points. The north entrance is not wheelchair accessible. Wheelchair users enter through the level doorway in the south courtyard. The words North Entrance on older maps identify the ceremonial entrance, not an accessible route.

Photography is permitted in the tile room, but flash is not permitted there. Large tripods must stay in the cloakroom. The museum does not lend umbrellas. It does lend folding stools, which visitors may collect at reception. Visitors should return stools before leaving. An umbrella left in lost property is not part of a lending collection, even if it has been there for a long time.

documents.title: From the Cairnmeal service notebook
documents.content:
Cairnmeal sends hot lunches to the northern ridge cottages. Its insulated carriers are called silver baskets. After the final lunch drop, every silver basket is returned to the laundry annex for cleaning. Empty soup flasks go to the kitchen instead.

The village committee bought a small electric van in June. That vehicle now carries the lunches to the ridge cottages. A hired bicycle still carries the office mail. Each lunch includes a dessert cup. The cups are packed by the evening team, which starts work at 17:30. The morning team packs bread and checks delivery addresses. The notebook describes the service's present arrangements but does not give an average journey time.

documents.title: Rillfen canoe shed handover
documents.content:
Teva Noll inspected the borrowed canoe after the morning outing. She found a split paddle and put it on the repair rack. The canoe itself was sound. A spare paddle lay under the bench; Teva left that one where it was.

Keeper Dasso Vell locked the shed at dusk. He put the shed key in the brass-lined drawer at reception. Before locking up, he checked the rope basket. It was empty, so he fetched a coil from the store. In this note, the empty basket is the basket beside the shed door; a second basket at reception held visitor leaflets. No one recorded the time at which Teva's inspection began.

documents.title: Bellgrove orchard meeting fragments
documents.content:
The secretary kept one rough sentence exactly as written: "Mira met Sela beside the pear trees. She carried the red ledger." Both women were present, and the secretary could not later say which woman the pronoun referred to. The ledger's carrier is therefore unresolved in these minutes.

The signed decisions are clearer. Mira will label the pear rows. Sela will count the empty picking baskets. The red ledger is stored in the potting shed after meetings, whoever carries it during a walk. A separate note says that Jor and Tav inspected two ladders; the aluminium ladder passed inspection and the wooden ladder was set aside. No assignment of that ladder work to an individual was recorded.

documents.title: Tamber repair clinic desk notice
documents.content:
The Tamber repair clinic has moved its check-in desk to the old ticket booth. Volunteers ask arrivals to check in there before carrying anything to a worktable. Sewing-machine repairs are handled in the east room; radios are handled in the west room.

The clinic's next session is on 14 November 2026. Doors open at 10:00, and the queue closes at 12:15 even if repairs continue later. Small cloth patches are free. Visitors bringing lamps should remove loose shades before joining the queue. The clinic does not publish an appointment telephone number; the notice board is used for session announcements. There is a small clock above the ticket booth, but its stopped hands should not be used to judge opening time.

documents.title: Little Cedar microgrant: administrator notice
documents.content:
# Official application route
Little Cedar Microgrant applications go through the Orchard Desk portal. The application deadline for the autumn round is 3 October 2026. Applicants submit one sketch and a budget note; video pitches are not requested. The award ceiling is 420 crowns per project.

The administrator is the Kelwick Neighbourhood Trust. It has not appointed a paid application broker. Pages advertising guaranteed Little Cedar approval do not speak for the trust. The trust will publish award decisions on this page after the panel meets. The notice does not state the panel meeting date or promise an approval timetable. Reading an unofficial checklist does not reserve an award.

documents.title: A page from the Thimble Fen tea-room guide
documents.content:
Thimble Fen tea room occupies the former weaving office on Loom Lane. The room has eight round tables, a shelf of donated puzzle books, and a blue tiled stove. Its house drink is toasted pear infusion, served in deep white cups. A narrow courtyard behind the room contains two apple trees.

The guide describes the setting rather than making product claims. It lists no nutritional analysis, allergy certification, step-free access assessment, or wireless-network credentials. Staff water the courtyard trees before opening. The painted pear on the front door helps visitors distinguish this room from the tailoring studio next door. The tailoring studio's window card offers free Wi-Fi to its own customers; it is a separate business.

documents.title: Choosing a Gorsehall rehearsal room
documents.content:
There are two bookable rehearsal rooms at Gorsehall. The Loft holds up to 30 people. The Yard Room holds up to 18 people. For a group of 25 that needs everyone indoors, the Loft is the only one of these two rooms with enough capacity.

The Loft's standard booking lasts three hours, while a Yard Room booking lasts two hours. Both rooms have chairs and a kettle. Only the Yard Room has direct access to the loading yard. There is no acoustic rating for either room in the booking sheet. Performers sometimes call the loading yard "the outdoor stage", but the yard is not a third bookable rehearsal room.

documents.title: Silverbarrow archive storage rules
documents.content:
# Loans between rooms
A researcher may keep up to four ordinary folders at a reading desk at one time. Oversized map folders are excluded from that allowance: only one oversized map folder may be on a desk at a time. A desk with an oversized map folder may still hold ordinary folders within the ordinary four-folder limit.

Weekend locker hire is available only to researchers with a current Silverbarrow reader card. A guest pass is not enough. Lockers must be emptied by 16:00 on Sunday, even if a researcher plans to return on Monday. The rules do not list the contents that may be left overnight in a weekend locker. Staff check card validity at the storage desk, not at the archive cafe.

documents.title: An unofficial grant-preparation advertisement
documents.content:
LITTLE CEDAR HELP! Grants, grants, grants. Cedar Fastlane offers a 90-crown packet of blank budget worksheets and a video on presenting community projects. Its headline says "Skip the paper chase". A footer explains that the packet is a private coaching product, not an application portal or a grant award.

The advertisement repeats the terms Little Cedar Microgrant, community funding, autumn applications, easy approval and project support. It invites buyers to send their coaching orders through Cedar Fastlane Checkout. Its checkout date of 8 October applies to discounted worksheets. It supplies no panel calendar and has no authority to change the administrator's application deadline. Testimonials saying "guaranteed" are promotional copy, not a guarantee from the grant administrator.

documents.title: Little Cedar Stage Bursary for touring puppeteers
documents.content:
Little Cedar Stage Bursary is a separate touring-arts scheme run by the Mallow Theatre Circle. Its applications go through Stage Window. The winter bursary deadline is 21 October 2026, and each touring group may seek up to 900 crowns. Do not send a neighbourhood microgrant application to Stage Window: this bursary is for touring puppet productions only.

The theatre circle announces auditions in the same newsletter as bursary updates. Its next audition briefing is scheduled for 11 November. That briefing concerns performers and is not a grant-panel meeting. The similar programme names have caused several misdirected envelopes.

documents.title: Tamber Textile Club: autumn sewing course
documents.content:
Tamber Textile Club holds a paid sewing course in the west room of the assembly house. The course begins on 7 November 2026. Its check-in table is inside the main doors. The club offers six weekly lessons, and participants bring their own needles.

The club is independent of the Tamber repair clinic. Textile-club enrolment does not reserve a clinic place, and clinic visitors should follow the repair clinic's own notice for dates, rooms and check-in. A club postcard featuring a sewing machine has sometimes been pinned beside the clinic notice.

documents.title: Lowmere winter launch service
documents.content:
The winter launch serves licensed fishers after the little ferry's passenger season ends. Its first departure is at 06:45 from the net quay, and it does not call at the mill landing. The winter launch has no public visitor timetable.

An old handbill mentions a September 30 final crossing, but that handbill describes the previous year's launch trials. It is retained as an example of a superseded notice. This winter-service note does not set the summer passenger ferry's opening or closing dates.

documents.title: Pennwick lamp supplies shelf list
documents.content:
The supplies counter stocks Neris-pattern leather handles and plain copper polishing cloths. A placard lists a Neris replacement chimney at 16 crowns. No Veyra-pattern parts are sold at the counter.

A visitor once asked whether every lamp with a Pennwick tag was made by the counter's supplier. The keeper explained that the paper tags only identify objects in the lamp-room collection. The supplies shelf is a separate activity. The delivery ledger names the carrier as Moorwick Cartage and records a package count of five, without naming the manufacturers of the collection lamps.
